value.rationale: The Witt class is the canonical invariant of a nondegenerate binary symmetric multiplication form, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Its square-class change shifts the local-derivation dimension from five to seven while the derivation dimension remains four. Most importantly, a concrete local map over a nonsplit field fails locality after separable base change, so the result captures a substantive arithmetic instability invisible in the complex classification. Complete finite-field formulas and exact linear 2-local rigidity give a natural closed low-dimensional picture.
